alternatives.label: Software, systems and algorithms
alternatives.concept: Combine programming, software construction, relational databases, networks and operating systems with algorithms, mathematical foundations, data and learning methods. Robotics and linear-system modelling add computational engineering applications. User-oriented product methods and general philosophical, ethical and communication work complement the computing core. Dedicated computer architecture, technical security, formal software specification and the full compulsory engineering-project sequence remain gaps.

alternatives.label: Computational modelling & statistical learning
alternatives.concept: Combine programming, software development, databases and algorithms with advanced calculus, linear systems, numerical analysis, probability, machine learning and reinforcement-learning agents. Empirical research and experimental-statistics courses place additional weight on model evaluation and quantitative inquiry; their project topics are not necessarily computing. This is a mathematical and statistical direction within computing, with less network and systems-engineering breadth.

blocks: Introduction to Programming directly addresses programming fundamentals, with different language and project scope.
Logic & Discrete Mathematics directly addresses formal reasoning, set theory and discrete structures.
UCR combines logic and discrete mathematics in one selected course, which is aligned once rather than duplicated across two TU/e components.
Software Development addresses software design, implementation and testing, but not TU/e’s complete engineering sequence.
Algorithms & Data Structures directly addresses data structures and introductory algorithmic design.
Advanced Algorithms develops algorithm analysis and design beyond the introductory UCR course.

UCR Algorithms & Data Structures includes finite-automata string matching, Turing machines, computability and complexity. It is allocated to Data Structures and does not establish full dedicated automata/formal-language coverage.
UCR has software development but no separate selected course dedicated to formal software specification.
Computer systems, data management and security
UCR has no selected course dedicated to computer architecture and organisation.
Shared relational-database content includes relational theory, normalization, SQL, authorization and query processing. This relationship does not imply identical coverage of database implementation.
Networks & Operating Systems directly addresses network design and operation, with broader combined scope.
Networks & Operating Systems is already aligned to Networks and is not duplicated; TU/e has a separate operating-systems course.
Partial technology-ethics relationship through normative theories, privacy, fairness, responsibility and human-AI/social consequences. TU/e retains its wider engineering ITEC programme.
AI Ethics addresses responsible computing but does not reproduce TU/e’s technical security course.
Mathematical Methods develops calculus-based methods used for computational modelling, with different breadth.
Linear Algebra directly addresses vectors, matrices and computational linear methods.

Direct probability/statistical-method relationship through probability spaces, distributions, estimation, hypothesis tests and Bayesian reasoning, with a sampling-algorithm project. It is not limited to introductory empirical-research design.
Introduction to Data Science addresses data collection, handling, analysis and visualisation, at a broader introductory level.
Machine Learning directly addresses supervised and unsupervised learning methods within TU/e’s combined statistics-and-ML component.

Partial heuristic/optimization-method relationship through search, local/global/population methods, constraints, implementation and experiments. TU/e also includes ILP/SAT solving and a dedicated capstone structure.
Human-centred design, communication and responsible technology
Academic formation, engineering projects and research

Partial robotics relationship through computational motion planning, collision avoidance and robot-arm programming. TU/e instead develops a mobile-robot digital twin in a team; UCR does not reproduce that complete cyber-physical project.
UCR is interdisciplinary but does not reproduce TU/e’s dedicated multidisciplinary engineering challenge course.
TU/e retains 45 EC of elective choice, subject to level, prior-knowledge and approval conditions. No fixed elective package is assumed here.
UCR has no 10-EC compulsory group Software Engineering project.
TU/e requires a 10-EC individual computer-science research project. UCR optional independent research is shown separately and is outside the scheduled 180 EC.
UCR ethics and social-science courses appear elsewhere, but no course is duplicated against this engineering-and-society component.

notes.text: TU/e CSE includes dedicated Computer Systems, Automata and Formal Languages, Software Specification, Operating Systems, Security, autonomous-systems and multidisciplinary CBL courses, a compulsory 10-EC Software Engineering project, a choice of advanced capstone and a 10-EC individual research-oriented Bachelor Final Project. UCR offers substantial programming, databases, systems, algorithms, mathematics, data science and AI, but neither alternative reproduces that complete engineering and project sequence. TU/e also preserves 45 EC of genuine elective space.

trace: Actual consumer-needs interviews, specifications, concept choice, quantitative product models, prototypes/fabrication and circularity/cost analysis. Complementary user-oriented physical-product methods, not a guaranteed software interface or HCI project.

Empirical research design, sampling/surveys/experiments and R-based inference/regression in a real research project. Complementary scientific evaluation methods; no computing dataset or independent computer-science thesis guaranteed.

Actual C++ and functional Haskell development, software design/quality, version control, review, debugging, testing, documentation and design patterns, with projects in both languages. Not the full external real-customer team-engineering sequence.

Actual algorithm/data-structure design, asymptotics, sorting/search/graphs and experimental performance inquiry, plus computability/Turing machines/verification/reductions/complexity. These latter contributions are recognised without claiming a separate complete formal-languages module.

Rigorous probability/statistical inference, distributions, estimation, Bayesian reasoning and MonteCarlo/random-sampling project. Strongest selected probability/statistics relationship; broader scientific-research methods are not substituted for mathematical probability.

General philosophical argument reconstruction/evaluation through historical and contemporary questions, including AI consciousness. Complementary conceptual humanities formation, not a philosophy-of-computing specialisation.

Actual experimental/multivariable statistical models, diagnostics, effect size/power and R data-analysis papers/poster in health/behavioural contexts. Transferable empirical validation methods, not guaranteed technical usability studies or AI training research.
Actual rhetorical analysis, argumentation, debate, speech and storytelling practice. Complementary academic/professional communication, not a technical software-documentation course.

Description-only AdvancedCalculus extends calculus to multidimensional/differential-equation/complex-valued settings with computer algebra for science/data analysis. Full stated contribution, without inventing absent outline details.

Actual robot-motion computation, transformations/kinematics, collision-free planning/manipulation, robot-arm/gripper programming and inverse-kinematics research. Human-robot/legal/ethical issue is a smaller component, not sustained HCI or CPU architecture.

audience.programmeDescription: This English-taught TU/e degree studies software systems and web services through programming, mathematical reasoning, algorithms, data and computer systems. It combines taught foundations with engineering projects, professional development and an individual final research project.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The first UCR programme emphasises software, networks, algorithms and computational engineering applications. The second gives more weight to mathematical models, statistical learning and empirical methods. Both offer related computer-science capacities, with gaps in dedicated computer architecture, technical security, formal software specification and TU/e’s compulsory engineering-project sequence.

curriculum.limitation: One of three capstones is shown, selected by official order. Places are limited. Elective choices and project topics require the applicable approval and prior knowledge; current offerings and requirements may change.

componentNotes.elective-space: 45 EC of elective choice: at most 15 EC at introductory level and at least 15 EC at advanced level, with no content overlap. Submit the planned programme for examination-board approval after earning 90 EC; changes require renewed approval. No fixed elective package is assumed.
componentNotes.y3-capstone: One 5-EC capstone is required. This example uses Heuristic Algorithms; places are limited and registration is first come, first served.
componentNotes.y3-se-project: This 10-EC course spans quarters 1–2 and combines software-engineering study with a real-customer team project. Software Specification normally precedes entry; the displayed sequence meets this. The current course page requires enrolment by 15 July; check the applicable year’s deadline.
componentNotes.y3-bep: This required 10-EC individual research project spans quarters 3–4. Entry requires 120 EC, all compulsory first-year courses and the applicable computer-science credits and topic preparation. The displayed prior-major sequence meets the stated 95-EC computer-science requirement.
componentNotes.y1-itec-ethics: The normal first-year study-advice threshold is 45 of 60 EC, with applicable personal circumstances considered. SCOP/e and Alumni Night, at least five Studium Generale activities and MyFuture activities with a total value of seven are additional completion requirements; they do not add credits to the 180 EC shown.
